title: Money and shopping
intro: Prices use costar and valer, both irregular. The currency changes by country — el peso in Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Chile, el sol in Peru, el euro in Spain — but the words for buying and paying do not.

entries.note: Uncountable: no dineros. la plata is everyday slang for money across much of Latin America.

ex.en: I haven't got any cash on me.
Prices went up again.

entries.en: to cost; to be hard, to take effort

ex.en: How much does the ticket cost?
I find it hard to get up early.

entries.note: ir de compras is to go shopping; las compras the shopping.

ex.en: I bought bread and milk.

entries.note: se vende on a sign means for sale.

ex.en: They sell fruit on the corner.

entries.note: Takes no preposition for the thing: pagar la cuenta. Use por only for an amount: pagué mil por el boleto.

ex.en: Can I pay by card?

entries.note: For spending time use pasar, not gastar.

ex.en: We spent too much on the trip.

ex.es: Gastó los zapatos en un mes.
ex.en: He wore the shoes out in a month.

ex.es: Es más barato en el mercado.
ex.en: It's cheaper at the market.
That hotel is extremely expensive.

entries.note: tarjeta de crédito, tarjeta de débito. A playing card is una carta.

ex.en: I lost my card.

entries.note: en efectivo is in cash. el cambio is change, both the coins and the act.

ex.en: They only take cash.
Keep the change.
There was a change of plan.

ex.es: El cambio está muy malo hoy.
ex.en: The exchange rate is very bad today.

entries.note: Also darse cuenta, to realise — a completely separate use of the same word.

ex.en: We asked for the bill.

ex.es: Transfirió el dinero a otra cuenta.
ex.en: He transferred the money to another account.

entries.note: Sales are las rebajas in Spain, las ofertas or la barata in Latin America.

ex.es: Nos dieron un descuento del diez por ciento.
ex.en: They gave us a ten per cent discount.
Would you like a bag?
The stock market fell yesterday.

entries.note: la factura is an invoice, and the word you need to claim expenses.

ex.es: Guarda el recibo por si acaso.
ex.en: Keep the receipt just in case.

entries.note: See also unit 8, where the same word means bench.

ex.es: Tengo que ir al banco antes de que cierre.
ex.en: I have to go to the bank before it closes.

entries.note: pedir prestado is to borrow. Spanish has no single verb for borrowing.

ex.en: Will you lend me your car?

entries.note: Same verb as must — see unit 1.

ex.en: I still owe him the money.

entries.note: rico also means delicious of food — see unit 7.

ex.en: He's from a wealthy family.
He grew up in a poor neighbourhood.
The market is open on Sundays.
The market is in crisis.
